findings.reason: the node would implement a check reading a pointer that does not exist for one of its two arms, so §6 must name the observable source of a shadow partner's non-terminal state (its run-dir record, or a pointer the paired dispatch is required to publish) for the primary arm's hold to have anything to read.
findings.text: §6 says the refusal reads "the partner's run id and phase", and its done-when (:245) requires "promoting a paired arm whose partner's pointer is `working` … succeeds once the partner's pointer is terminal", but §5 (:217-218) states that a shadow lineage publishes no launch pointer and that "its record is written only at the end of its own dispatch", and `_publish_launch_claim` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:576) suppresses the pointer for `shadow_lineage` ("A shadow run publishes nothing"), so when the arm being promoted is the primary arm its partner is the shadow, whose pointer — the only source §6 names — does not exist for the whole of that arm's life; the hold would silently never fire in that direction, which is exactly the "first arm to land" case §6's Why states it exists to close

response_events.reason: the premise does not hold: dispatch.py:2046 writes a shadow's full live pointer unconditionally; only the pre-launch scope claim (_publish_launch_claim, and the scope check under if not shadow_lineage) is skipped. A shadow's pointer exists from launch until promotion, so s6 can read the partner's phase in both directions. s5's 'publishes no launch pointer' should read 'launch claim'; that wording is fixed before s5 dispatches (comment c-s5-claim-not-pointer)
